 LIFESTYLE Personal Finance Average Social Security check at age 65: How much will you get for 2027 with the COLA for next year?
 A 3.6% increase is coming to Social Security benefits in 2027, but how much extra can Americans turning 65 expect to receive?
 Social Security Administration 
 BRANDON SUTTON (SAM)
 Editor Editor Updated 14/11/2026
 -
 06:08 CST 
 Follow MARCA on Google

 Personal Finance.  Can you just walk into a Social Security office without an appointment? These are the few cases when you can do it 
 US News.  Mega Millions Winning Numbers: Results for this Friday, November 13 drawing for the $555 Million Jackpot 
 According to the Social Security Administration (SSA) , the average monthly retirement benefit for Americans aged 65 was $1607.27 in December 2025 and applying the newly announced 3.6% Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) would increase that figure by approximately $57.86 for retirees.
Bringing the estimated monthly payment to $1665.13 in 2027, the calculation provides a useful indication of what age-65 beneficiaries could receive next year, although it is not an official forecast of payments for everyone turning 65 in 2027 whilst individual benefits are determined by personal earnings records and retirement decisions. 
 Hidden beneath California’s cliffs: The mysterious cave that may hold prohibition-era secrets There is also a noticeable difference between what men and women currently receive at this age as SSA figures put the average monthly payment for men aged 65 at $1772, compared with $1457.40 for women – and if the same COLA is applied, those amounts would rise to approximately $1835.79 and $1509.87, respectively.
Although reaching 65 marks an important milestone because of Medicare eligibility, it does not mean Americans automatically qualify for their full Social Security retirement benefit as anyone born in 1960 or later has a full retirement age of 67, and claiming at 65 results in a reduction of approximately 13.33% compared to waiting two extra years.
Additionally, those who postpone claiming beyond their Full Retirement Age receive delayed retirement credits, increasing their monthly payments by approximately 8% for each additional year until age 70. 
 The COLA change could benefit retirees LAPRESSE What else is changing for Social Security in 2027?
 The SSA calculates retirement benefits using a worker's 35 highest-earning years, adjusted for inflation. Consequently, two people retiring at the same age can receive substantially different monthly payments depending on their employment and earnings histories.
However, that does not necessarily make waiting the right decision for everyone as someone facing financial difficulties, limited retirement savings or health concerns may prefer to begin receiving payments earlier rather than delay access to that income.
The 3.6% COLA is not the only adjustment coming next year as the SSA has also announced changes to several important thresholds affecting beneficiaries and workers. For example, the maximum amount of annual earnings subject to Social Security payroll taxes will increase from $184,500 in 2026 to $192,300 in 2027.
Meanwhile, beneficiaries who have not reached full retirement age can earn up to $25,560 annually before the retirement earnings test begins withholding payments as the maximum monthly benefit for someone retiring at full retirement age will also increase from $4152 to $4188.
Ultimately, the estimated $1665 monthly payment provides a useful benchmark for understanding what the 2027 adjustment could mean for 65-year-old beneficiaries. However, anyone approaching retirement should check their individual benefit estimate through their my Social Security account before deciding when to claim.
The difference between retiring at 65, 67 or 70 could have a lasting impact on household finances, making the timing of that decision just as important as the annual COLA increase.
